## 開篇固定收益論點

美國固定收益市場8月19日收盤的主軸，是政策帶動長端上漲，而非存續期間問題獲得根本解決。2年期美債殖利率持平於4.19%，5年期下滑2個基點至4.35%，10年期下滑6個基點至4.65%，30年期則下滑9個基點至5.19%。2年期與10年期利差因而收窄6個基點至46個基點，2年期與30年期利差收窄9個基點至100個基點；前一交易日尾盤才初步企穩，先前承受全球債市賣壓的年期隨即轉為強勁反彈。觸媒格外直接：美國財政部長Scott Bessent宣布，10年至30年期債券的流動性支持回購規模將至少加倍；就在兩週前，例行季度融資計畫才維持原有規模不變。

走勢結構清楚顯示政策改變了什麼，又未改變什麼。10年期實質殖利率下滑6個基點至2.35%，完全解釋10年期名目殖利率的跌幅，10年期損益兩平通膨率則持平於2.30%。30年期名目殖利率下滑9個基點，也與實質殖利率下降9個基點一致。財政部降低民間市場邊際上預期必須承接的存續期間，並顯示官方對長期借貸成本設有容忍臨界點；但政策並未帶來新的通膨降溫訊號。過去1個月，30年期殖利率仍上升13個基點，10年期上升10個基點，損益兩平通膨率也上升6個基點。因此，長存續期間債券確實獲得舒緩，但行情仍有賴官方持續支持，或後續通膨、成長、財政政策或供給情勢改善。

政策背景限制這波行情的延伸幅度。聯準會7月會議紀要顯示，決策以9比3通過將政策利率維持在3.5%至3.75%；Lorie Logan、Beth Hammack與Neel Kashkari主張升息25個基點而投下反對票。數名官員傾向緊縮，許多人表示若通膨未下降，就有必要升息，即使多數人預期關稅與先前能源價格上漲的影響將在今年剩餘期間消退。會後公布的就業疲弱、核心通膨放緩，以及7月零售銷售大幅下降，已降低9月採取行動的急迫性；但會議紀要揭示的鷹派陣營比表決結果更廣，無投票權的Jeff Schmid與Alberto Musalem也表示會支持升息。2年期殖利率不變、長端上漲，反映市場接受財政部干預存續期間，卻未獲得聯準會反應函數明確轉向寬鬆的訊號。

跨資產價格將這項宣布解讀為實質金融壓力減輕及對美元的挑戰，而非經濟衰退的證據。美元指數下跌0.82%至98.831，創3個月低點；黃金期貨上漲4.69%至$4,570.90。標普500指數上漲0.21%，VIX下跌6.00%至14.89，但那斯達克100指數下跌0.22%，半導體指數下跌2.12%。這種分歧值得注意。財政部支持降低主權債券的折現率，卻未消除市場對AI投資週期成本、規模與預期回報的疑慮。阿拉伯聯合大公國切斷與伊朗的經濟關係後，布蘭特原油仍上漲0.60%至$91.57，WTI則下跌0.67%至$84.37。地緣政治升溫之際，損益兩平通膨率仍然穩定，油價管道因而未能逆轉債市漲勢；這也意味實質殖利率的變動不能視為廣泛的通膨重新定價。

信用市場運作正常，也受惠於存續期間行情。LQD上漲0.69%，HYG與JNK均上漲約0.23%；這些基金價格反映總報酬韌性，而非現券利差變動。更關鍵的證據來自初級市場。Alphabet完成首次澳幣發債，規模A$55億，高於最初規畫的約A$50億，認購需求逾A$180億。其20年期券殖利率為6.98%，是該公司歷來債券融資中最高的票息等值借款成本；同時，Nebius新發行$45億可轉債，加上一筆與Anthropic相關、規模$160億的德州專案融資，讓同一輪融資週期進一步延伸至權益敏感及次順位結構。市場仍能提供大規模資金，但資金價格與風險配置正成為關鍵約束。

## 財政部護盤遇上$40兆資產負債表

財政部在季度中途介入，直接處理價格已趨不穩的年期區段，因此扭轉收盤走勢，即使市場交易仍然有序。財政部表示，將把10年至30年期債券的流動性支持回購規模至少加倍，擴大後的操作自9月9日開始。先前公布的暫定日程截至11月4日，該區段回購金額最高為$140億；規模加倍代表至少再增加$140億。Barclays估計，每季將額外回購約$160億，相當於20年期與30年期公債全年供給量約15%。在8月交投清淡的環境下，邊際影響相當可觀，但相較於規模達數十兆美元的市場，仍不足以主導公允價值。

政策訊號的力量大於實際金額。回購參數通常隨季度再融資計畫公布，財政部僅在兩週前才重申維持原有規模。兩次再融資計畫之間臨時調整日程，等於告訴投資人，30年期殖利率升破5.30%已跨越官方容忍門檻。政府反應函數也因此成為長端估值的一環：若再度出現賣壓，市場如今可能預期回購規模進一步調整，或標售規模最終改變。30年期殖利率降至5.19%、10年期降至4.65%，顯示投資人起初是回補空單並下調預期淨存續期間，而非改變對政策利率的看法。

現券交易活動讓價格反應更有實質依據。美債按原始面額計算的成交量達$1.370兆，較前一交易日增加28.1%；其中名目附息債成交$1.112兆，增加31.5%。7年至10年期區段成交量增加53.1%至$2,343億，20年以上年期成交$1,707億，增加52.0%。交易商對客戶交易分別占這兩個區段的39.9%與46.0%。數據無法判定客戶是淨買方或淨賣方，但這波漲勢是在雙向交投異常活躍之下形成，而非流動性缺席所致。20年以上政府債券指數上漲1.69%，遠高於1年至3年期指數的0.03%報酬，確認重新定價集中於存續期間。

回購融資也衍生第二層年期配置交易。財政部未說明如何籌措擴大回購的資金，但國庫券通常是調節工具。Wells Fargo估計，若每季持續回購$320億，至11月5日前可能需要額外發行約$120億國庫券，此後每季則需增加$160億。相較於每月接近$2.25兆的國庫券標售總額，這些金額不大，重要的是方向：民間投資人持有的存續期間減少，代價卻是再融資曝險提高，日後國庫券供給也更難預測。操作改變政府利率風險的分布，並未消除造成舉債需求的赤字。

同一天，財政約束變得更加清晰。截至週二收盤，公共債務達$40.05兆，較2022年1月高出三分之一。本會計年度迄今利息支出為$1.17兆，較上年同期增加15%，並已成為僅次於醫療保健與社會安全的第3大預算項目。今年前10個月財政赤字為$1.8兆，較一年前擴大5%，債務上限則為$41.1兆。債務跨越整數門檻，本身既不是違約觸發點，也不是估值模型；但殖利率上升會增加利息支出，進而推高未來融資需求，使下一波殖利率升勢更難承受。

因此，這波漲勢不能解讀為期限溢價重新定價已告終。政府每年赤字仍接近$2兆，財政部只是從市場收回部分長債。若投資人認為長期利率下滑源自行政治理，而非通膨下降或財政可信度增強所給予的補償，回購也可能削弱美元。週三實質殖利率下降、損益兩平通膨率不變、美元下跌0.82%的組合，符合這項解讀。黃金上漲4.69%，更反映官方行動在未改變債務軌跡的情況下降低美債實質報酬後，市場轉向替代性價值儲藏工具。

制度成本較難衡量，但仍不可忽視。規律且可預測的發債安排，長期以來有助降低美國財政融資承擔的風險溢價。意外修訂可在當下支撐價格，卻也降低未來供給指引的可靠性；若投資人推斷11月選舉前的政治目標正在影響年期管理，影響尤其明顯。這層矛盾並不否定回購的流動性功能：舊券與非指標券的流動性低於當期指標券，財政部也一向收到大量優質報價。但未來成效取決於政策一致性。若政策反覆干預，卻沒有赤字放緩、通膨降溫或民間發債減少配合，市場可能再次測試同一個長端門檻。

## 通膨約束仍由聯準會主導

7月會議紀要凸顯財政部希望降低長期利率，與聯準會抗通膨任務尚未完成之間的落差。Logan、Hammack與Kashkari反對維持利率不變，使本次決策成為連續5次會議未調整利率後，這一輪首度出現的9比3表決。數名決策官員傾向升息，許多人指出，若通膨未下降，政策就必須進一步緊縮。多數人預期，隨關稅影響及先前能源價格上漲效應消退，通膨將逐步下降；但19名決策官員中近半數認為，通膨可能更具黏著性。伊朗戰爭又使前景更加混濁。

會後公布的數據，走勢與這些鷹派風險相反。企業7月裁減人力，前兩個月新增就業遭下修，核心通膨溫和，零售銷售則創一年多來最大跌幅。會議紀要公布前，期貨定價隱含9月升息機率約36%，低於7月底逾70%的水準。紀要形容勞動市場穩定且均衡，資本投資與生產力仍然強勁，因此數據尚不足以證明經濟收縮；但這些資料確實解釋，為何會議紀要揭露更多官員偏好緊縮後，2年期殖利率仍持平於4.19%。

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh提議將每年例行政策會議由8次減至6次，另添政策反應速度的不確定性。今年會議次數不會改變，減少會議可讓每次決策之間累積更多資訊；但能源、關稅與地緣政治情勢快速變化時，也可能提高每場會議的事件風險。就8月19日收盤而言，這項提案的重要性不及背後的溝通問題：投資人仍須判斷Warsh究竟把偏高的長期殖利率視為有益的緊縮力量、財政與可信度風險的訊號，還是兩者兼具。財政部回購明確以壓低這些殖利率為目標，形成債務管理者放鬆長端、央行卻維持有條件緊縮傾向的政策組合。

市場分解顯示，週三財政部的行動本身並未放鬆通膨約束。即使實質殖利率降至2.35%，10年期損益兩平通膨率仍為2.30%，過去1週上升4個基點。阿拉伯聯合大公國遭受疑似飛彈攻擊後，停止與伊朗的貿易及金融交易；布蘭特原油收於$91.57，過去1週上漲2.91%。伊朗否認涉案，航班仍持續運行。Saudi Aramco保證至少3家歐洲煉油商9月原油供應量全數到位，帶來部分實體供給緩衝。WTI與布蘭特收盤走勢分歧，加上損益兩平通膨率不變，顯示能源仍是有效的尾端風險，而非推動美債漲勢的邊際因素。

房市說明，決策官員不能只把長期殖利率下降視為抽象的市場事件。30年期房貸平均利率仍為6.67%，伊朗衝突前則低於6%；7月成屋待完成銷售量，與2001年開始統計以來的第二低點相當。Redfin估計賣方比買方多51.3%，成屋價格中位數仍接近6月創下的$434,000紀錄，獨棟住宅開工則降至2022年以來最低。若美債殖利率持續走低，可減輕融資壓力；但交易量與住宅營建疲弱，也警示貨幣緊縮正以不均衡的方式傳導。聯準會面對的是利率敏感產業疲弱、資本支出強勁、能源通膨未解的經濟，而非方向一致的需求訊號。

風險資產也做出相同區分。標普500指數上漲0.21%、VIX下降，顯示回購並未引發衰退疑慮。半導體股再跌2.12%，過去1週跌幅擴至5.33%，因為政府債券的存續期間成本下降，無法回答AI營收是否足以支撐相關債務與股權資本。前端殖利率不變，美元指數卻下跌，顯示投資人把寬鬆效果歸因於年期管理，而非美國成長優勢變得更明確。對聯準會而言，若美元持續走弱，也可能使通膨路徑更加複雜。

## AI資本進入新的風險層級

Alphabet將先前推向市場的澳洲融資計畫落實為A$55億交易，為與主權債存續期間競爭的頂級企業發行人，提供最清楚的當前定價。認購金額超過A$180億。公司發行A$10億20年期債券，殖利率6.98%，較當地指標利率高180個基點；最大一檔為A$15億浮動利率券，認購需求也最高。相較於前一日的初步指引，新增資訊在於實際執行結果：這筆首次發債規模高於約A$50億的目標，但最長年期券仍創下Alphabet歷來最高的債券殖利率。

這筆交易同時呈現融資管道與傳導機制。Alphabet擁有標普第二高信用評等，以及企業中最強健的資產負債表之一，因此偏高的絕對殖利率主要反映全球主權債殖利率曲線，而非發行人本身惡化。同時，高評等的超大規模雲端服務商可提供足夠的額外殖利率，吸引核心固定收益需求從政府債券轉向企業債。公司預估2026年資本支出最高達$2,050億，並已透過美元、瑞士法郎、英鎊、歐元、加幣、日圓及如今的澳幣發債，顯示AI融資需求正觸及多個本地儲蓄池。主權殖利率決定基礎成本，科技業供給則在此之上增加競爭。

Nebius將風險移轉進一步推向股權。這家總部位於阿姆斯特丹的AI雲端公司推出兩檔、合計$45億可轉債：一檔規模$27.5億，2030年到期，擬定票息0%至0.5%；另一檔規模$17.5億，2034年到期，擬定票息4%至4.5%。公司今年稍早已發行約$43億可轉債；截至週二股價累計上漲197%後，這次消息使股價在美股開盤前一度下跌9.2%。轉換價值可降低現金票息，卻把部分融資成本轉為未來股權稀釋，也讓債權人承擔股權估值能否維持的風險。這筆交易預計要到週三稍晚才定價，因此行銷條件反映融資意圖，而非最終成交水準。

私募信貸承擔的結構性次順位更為明顯。Eagle Point Credit Management在Nexus Data Centers規模$160億的融資案中，提供約$13億夾層債務；資金用於Nexus位於德州Hubbard、占地2,900英畝的園區。Anthropic是主要承租戶，專案包括自有燃氣發電廠，Google則同意為優先債務提供擔保。Eagle Point的部位低於資本結構中最安全的層級。這筆融資起初是約$1.5億、以土地擔保的優先擔保債務；隨承租戶與擔保組合增強，規模多次擴大。

這套結構集中了多項相互依存的條件。工程必須完工、Anthropic必須使用該產能、專用發電資產必須具備經濟效益，而Google的擔保保護的是優先層級，不是夾層債權。開發商通常在完工後為建築貸款再融資，Nexus可能於今年稍晚尋求發行高收益債券，為銀行主導的$150億部分再融資。因此，專案可在實體完工後，從私募建築風險轉入公開信用市場，最終損失如何分配，仍取決於擔保範圍、抵押品價值與再融資條件。

即使週三債市上漲，整體發債日程仍龐大，足以與主權供給競爭。美國8月投資等級債發行量達$1,520億，連續第3個月創紀錄；歐洲借款人本週發行至少EUR385億，為歷來最繁忙的暑期後重啟。歐洲投資等級債利差週二收盤為77個基點，較6月底收窄；強勁的基金流入，使Finland、Sika、Mizuho等發行人即使面對政府債券賣壓，仍能順利發債。市場並未關閉。投資人要求合理的新券讓利，也愈來愈需要在存續期間、企業信用、專案執行、轉換權或次順位風險之間做出選擇。

8月19日的整體報酬，獎勵存續期間因子。美國20年以上AAA至A級企業債指數上漲1.61%，相應BBB級指數上漲1.51%，已開發市場10年以上投資等級美元債指數上漲1.35%。這些漲幅均低於長期美債指數的1.69%，也不能證明利差收窄。數據顯示，財政部介入透過指標利率管道推升長天期企業債，但發行人與結構選擇問題仍未解決。

擬議中的$11.5億Digital Drive債券，將在承租戶資質較弱的一端帶來後續考驗。這座維吉尼亞州資料中心出租給投機等級的CoreWeave；與CoreWeave相關的可比專案債務，殖利率明顯高於有藍籌超大規模雲端服務商支持的融資，Galaxy Digital 7月一筆$35億交易的利率達10%。9月發債仍在規畫中，但已界定AI信用市場的下一個問題：當承租戶信用、集中度與建築風險不變時，指標利率下降能否壓低專案票息。

## 政策分歧與債權人控制權

印尼方面，會前所述的按兵不動預期，如今已有實際決策結果。代理總裁Destry Damayanti將BI-Rate維持在5.75%，連續第2個月不變；今年以來則已累計升息100個基點。她重申匯率穩定是首要任務，擴大一項自9月第2週生效的避險獎勵計畫，並表示央行將持續干預境內外市場，同時運用總體審慎工具支持放款。印尼盾收盤升值0.1%，10年期政府債殖利率下滑5個基點至7.11%，為近2個月低點。

決策延續政策方向，但改變了工具。印尼央行希望吸引外幣資金，卻不提高SRBI證券殖利率；隨流通發行量減少，其12個月期平均殖利率在8月14日下滑22個基點。7月信貸成長達13.58%，至少為疫情以來最快，使央行有理由避免進一步收緊國內流動性。這套作法降低近期再次升息的機率，同時明確維持捍衛印尼盾的立場；但弱點也很清楚：若美元再度走強或美債殖利率上升，新領導層可能被迫在較低廉的國內流動性與匯率可信度之間取捨。

南非出現更明確的通膨降溫驚喜。7月整體通膨率由5.0%降至4.3%，低於市場共識4.5%；月增率由0.7%放緩至0.2%。商品通膨由4.8%降至3.4%，服務通膨由5.2%降至5.0%，食品通膨則降至0.6%，為2010年以來最低。核心通膨走勢相反，年增率由4.1%微升至4.2%，因此數據支持耐心觀望，而非無條件轉向寬鬆。10年期政府債殖利率下滑2個基點至8.68%；遠期利率協議仍反映9月23日會議升息25個基點的機率為70%。

印度8月3日至5日會議紀要也支持等待，但起點更明確偏鷹。6人委員會一致同意將附買回利率維持在5.25%，並連續第4次會議維持中性立場。總裁Sanjay Malhotra強調，食品、燃料及其他投入成本上漲可能擴散；副總裁Poonam Gupta則表示，由於預估10月至12月當季通膨將達5.9%，今年稍晚可能有必要升息。印度央行將本會計年度成長預測上調至6.7%，並將通膨預測下調至5%，保留觀察能源衝擊、而非立即反應的空間。

韓國殖利率曲線顯示，當長端通膨疑慮超過市場預期的央行行動時，會產生何種結果。3年期與10年期利差接近54個基點，為2021年10月以來最寬；10年期殖利率自2月底以來已上升約90個基點。投資人質疑韓國央行是否會在7月升息25個基點後積極緊縮，3年期殖利率因而已較7月底高點下滑13個基點。即使LS Securities預期今年只會再升息1次，並於2027年上半年達到3.25%的終端利率，對石油的依賴及全球主權債賣壓，仍使期限補償維持高檔。

新興市場信用提供兩種特質性韌性的案例。埃及主權美元債利差截至上週末降至322個基點，為2014年以來最低，且自3月以來約收窄150個基點。外匯存底創$563億紀錄，加上更具彈性的埃及鎊、僑匯、觀光、蘇伊士運河收入，以及IMF審查後撥付的$18億，均降低迫切的外部融資風險。總融資需求偏高與民營化進展緩慢仍是約束，這波漲勢也使估值緩衝縮小。相較之下，烏克蘭2029年到期債券殖利率為13%，價格接近85美分，已高於2025年6月的58美分。歐洲批准EUR900億貸款、軍事調整及債權人重整，改善市場對融資續航力的看法；但債務預估至2027年將達GDP的110%，攻擊事件則可能使穀物出口減半。該國主權債今年12%的報酬，是對戰爭與重整結果的補償，並非埃及交易的低風險版本。

AI以外的私募信貸損失，也具體呈現債權人控制權。現由BlackRock持有的HPS與Oaktree，將最高$9億債務轉換為約$1億股權，並再投入$4,000萬，藉此取得MBS Group控制權。HPS持有$6億第一順位留置權債權，Oaktree則持有$3億次順位留置權債權。借貸成本上升、影視製作活動減少，以及2023年勞資罷工重創攝影棚營運後，這項重整排除Hackman Capital Partners與Affinius Capital。減債可恢復營運能力，但債轉股也揭示企業價值損失的嚴重程度，並將債權回收來源由契約債權轉為持有景氣循環型製作服務企業的股權。

這些主權與企業案例，無法用單一全球存續期間結論概括。印尼以獎勵措施與針對性工具捍衛匯率；南非整體通膨降溫，但核心物價仍具黏著性；印度正在等待能源衝擊發展；韓國計入的油價與期限溢價高於可能的政策路徑；埃及重建外部緩衝；烏克蘭交易取決於援助與戰爭結果；MBS債權人則已接管公司。美國長期殖利率下降改善共同的折現率環境，但誰能受惠，仍由各地政策可信度、現金流控制權、抵押品與再融資結構決定。

## 前瞻市場意義

財政部干預能否持久，如今取決於回購宣布引發的初步空單回補結束後，操作是否仍能改變市場成交價格。9月9日開始操作、每次10年至30年期回購的最終規模、用於融資的國庫券發行，以及長期附息債標售指引是否修訂，都將顯示這項計畫仍是有限度的流動性措施，還是已轉為主動年期管理。若長端持續上漲、國庫券融資穩定且現券雙向交投活躍，將證明適度降低存續期間供給，足以吸引民間買盤回流。若擴大操作後，30年期殖利率仍回升至宣布前高點附近，焦點將重回$40.05兆債務餘額、$1.17兆利息支出，以及反覆突襲式干預造成的可信度成本。

下一輪通膨與政策訊號，必須調和聯準會7月會議紀要與會後轉弱的經濟活動。Warsh在Jackson Hole的談話，以及下一批就業、零售與通膨數據，需要顯示3名有投票權官員的反對票與2名鷹派無投票權官員，究竟代表持久的緊縮聯盟，還是已被疲弱數據超越的立場。若招聘與消費持續疲弱、核心物價保持穩定，將驗證2年期殖利率持平的合理性，並讓實質殖利率帶動的漲勢擴大。若服務通膨持續、美元走弱，或布蘭特原油明確升破目前$91.57的收盤價，前端將重新與長端連動，並凸顯財政部放寬金融條件與聯準會通膨使命之間的矛盾。

日本8月20日20年期公債標售，是檢驗美國債市舒緩能否傳導至其他主權殖利率曲線的最近一項外部測試。標售前殖利率接近3.775%，仍靠近7月3.89%的高點；市場認為日本央行9月升息機率約四分之三，國內機構對超長存續期間也態度審慎。投標倍數、標售尾差與次級市場表現，將區分買盤究竟是受到絕對殖利率吸引，還是僅承接美債帶來的短暫舒緩。若承接強勁，代表美國官方支持可在殖利率足夠高時，重新打開全球存續期間需求；若需求疲弱，則確認即使美國殖利率曲線趨平，日本貨幣政策正常化、財政立場與買方退場仍是獨立壓力。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The August 19 U.S. fixed-income close was a policy-induced long-end rally, not a fundamental resolution of the duration problem. The 2-year Treasury yield held at 4.19%, the 5-year fell 2 basis points to 4.35%, the 10-year declined 6 basis points to 4.65%, and the 30-year dropped 9 basis points to 5.19%. That move flattened 2s10s by 6 basis points to 46 and 2s30s by 9 basis points to 100, reversing the prior session's late stabilization into a much stronger rally at the maturities that had borne the global selloff. The catalyst was unusually direct: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that liquidity-support buybacks of 10- to 30-year securities would at least double, only two weeks after the regular quarterly financing schedule had left their size unchanged.

The composition of the move shows what the announcement changed and what it did not. The 10-year real yield fell 6 basis points to 2.35%, accounting for the entire decline in the nominal 10-year yield, while the 10-year breakeven held at 2.30%. At 30 years, the 9-basis-point nominal rally matched a 9-basis-point decline in the real yield. Treasury altered the amount of duration the private market expects to absorb at the margin and established an official pain point around long borrowing costs; it did not produce a new disinflation signal. The 30-year yield remains 13 basis points higher over 1 month, the 10-year is 10 basis points higher, and breakeven inflation is 6 basis points higher over that period. Long-duration relief was therefore real but contingent on continued official support or a later improvement in inflation, growth, fiscal policy or supply.

The policy backdrop limits how far that relief can extend. July Federal Reserve minutes showed a 9-3 vote to hold the policy rate at 3.5%-3.75%, with Lorie Logan, Beth Hammack and Neel Kashkari dissenting for a 25-basis-point increase. Several officials favored tightening and many said an increase would be necessary if inflation failed to decline, even as most expected tariff and earlier energy effects to fade over the rest of the year. Subsequent weak payrolls, softer core inflation and a sharp July retail-sales decline have reduced the urgency of a September move, but the minutes reveal a broader hawkish coalition than the vote alone: nonvoters Jeff Schmid and Alberto Musalem have also said they would have supported an increase. The unchanged 2-year yield alongside the long-end rally captures a market that accepted Treasury's duration intervention without receiving a clearly easier Fed reaction function.

Cross-asset prices treated the announcement as an easing in real financial pressure and a challenge to the dollar rather than as evidence of recession. The Dollar Index fell 0.82% to 98.831, its weakest level in three months, and gold futures rose 4.69% to $4,570.90. The S&P 500 gained 0.21% and the VIX fell 6.00% to 14.89, yet the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.22% and the semiconductor index declined 2.12%. That split matters. Treasury support relieved the sovereign discount rate, but it did not erase doubts about the cost, scale and prospective returns of the AI investment cycle. Brent still rose 0.60% to $91.57 after the United Arab Emirates cut economic ties with Iran, while WTI fell 0.67% to $84.37. Stable breakevens despite geopolitical escalation prevented the oil channel from defeating the rally; they also prevent the real-yield move from being called a broad inflation repricing.

Credit remained functional and benefited from the duration rally. LQD gained 0.69%, and HYG and JNK each rose about 0.23%; those fund prices describe total-return resilience, not a cash-spread move. The more consequential evidence came from the primary market. Alphabet completed a A$5.5 billion debut Australian-dollar deal, larger than the roughly A$5 billion initially contemplated, after more than A$18 billion of demand. Its 20-year tranche yielded 6.98%, the highest coupon-equivalent borrowing cost the company has paid on a note, while a new $4.5 billion Nebius convertible offering and a $16 billion Anthropic-linked Texas project financing extended the same funding cycle into equity-sensitive and subordinated structures. Capital is available in size. Its price and risk allocation are becoming the binding questions.

## Treasury Put Meets a $40 Trillion Balance Sheet

Treasury's mid-quarter intervention transformed the close because it addressed the exact maturity sector that had become unstable in price, even though trading conditions were orderly. The department said it would increase by at least double the liquidity-support buybacks for securities dated from 10 to 30 years, with the larger operations beginning September 9. Its earlier tentative calendar through November 4 contemplated as much as $14 billion of purchases in that sector; doubling implies at least another $14 billion, and Barclays estimated roughly $16 billion of additional purchases per quarter, or about 15% of annual 20- and 30-year supply. That is material at the margin, especially in thin August conditions, without being large enough to dictate fair value against a market measured in tens of trillions.

The signal was more powerful than the cash amount. Buyback parameters are normally communicated with the quarterly refunding, and Treasury had reaffirmed the existing size only two weeks earlier. Changing the schedule between refundings told investors that the rise in the 30-year yield above 5.30% had crossed an official tolerance threshold. It also made the government's reaction function part of long-end valuation: a renewed selloff may now encounter further adjustments to buybacks or eventual changes to auction sizes. The 30-year's drop to 5.19% and the 10-year's decline to 4.65% show that investors initially responded through short covering and reduced expected net duration rather than through a change in the policy rate.

Cash activity gives that price response substance. Treasury turnover reached $1.370 trillion in original-face par value, 28.1% above the prior session, with nominal coupons accounting for $1.112 trillion, up 31.5%. Activity in the 7- to 10-year bucket rose 53.1% to $234.3 billion, and more than 20-year maturities traded $170.7 billion, up 52.0%. Dealer-to-customer transactions represented 39.9% and 46.0% of those buckets, respectively. The data cannot identify whether customers were net buyers or sellers, but the rally was established amid unusually heavy two-way transfer rather than an absence of liquidity. The 20-plus-year government bond index gained 1.69%, substantially more than the 0.03% return in the 1- to 3-year index, confirming the concentration of the repricing in duration.

Funding the intervention creates a second-order maturity trade. Treasury did not specify how it would pay for the larger purchases, but bills are its normal balancing instrument. Wells Fargo estimated that a sustained buyback pace of $32 billion per quarter could require about $12 billion of extra bill issuance through November 5 and $16 billion per quarter thereafter. Those amounts are small against gross monthly bill auctions near $2.25 trillion. Their importance lies in the direction: less duration outstanding with private investors now comes with more refinancing exposure and less predictable bill supply later. The maneuver changes the distribution of the government's interest-rate risk; it does not retire the deficit that creates the borrowing.

That fiscal constraint became more visible on the same day. Public debt reached $40.05 trillion at Tuesday's close, one-third more than in January 2022. Fiscal-year-to-date interest expense stands at $1.17 trillion, 15% above the comparable prior-year period and already the third-largest budget category after healthcare and Social Security. The fiscal deficit through the first ten months of the year was $1.8 trillion, 5% wider than a year earlier, and the debt ceiling is $41.1 trillion. A round-number debt threshold is not itself a default trigger or valuation model, but rising yields increase interest expense, which raises future financing needs and makes the next yield increase harder to absorb.

This is why the rally cannot be interpreted as the end of the term-premium repricing. Treasury removed some long bonds from the market while the government continues to run an annual shortfall near $2 trillion. The operation may also weaken the dollar if investors view lower long rates as administratively induced rather than as compensation for lower inflation or stronger fiscal credibility. Wednesday's combination of falling real yields, an unchanged breakeven and a 0.82% dollar decline fits that interpretation. Gold's 4.69% gain reinforces the market's preference for an alternative store of value when official action lowers the real return on Treasuries without changing the debt trajectory.

The institutional cost is less measurable but still relevant. Regular and predictable issuance has long reduced the risk premium attached to Treasury financing. A surprise revision can support prices today while making future supply guidance less dependable, particularly if investors infer that political objectives ahead of the November elections influence maturity management. That tension does not invalidate the buyback's liquidity purpose: older, off-the-run securities are less liquid than current benchmarks, and Treasury routinely receives large volumes of high-quality offers. It does mean that future effectiveness depends on consistency. Repeated interventions that are not accompanied by slower deficits, softer inflation or reduced private issuance could invite the market to retest the same long-end threshold.

## The Fed Still Owns the Inflation Constraint

The July minutes sharpened the contrast between Treasury's desire for lower long rates and the Fed's incomplete inflation task. Logan, Hammack and Kashkari dissented from the hold, making the decision the first 9-3 vote in the current sequence after five consecutive meetings without a rate change. Several participants favored a hike, and many indicated that policy would need to tighten if inflation did not decline. Most expected inflation to step down as tariff effects and earlier energy increases faded, but nearly half of the 19 policymakers saw a risk of greater persistence. The Iran war further clouded that outlook.

Incoming data after the meeting have moved in the opposite direction from those hawkish risks. Employers cut jobs in July, hiring in the prior two months was revised lower, core inflation was subdued, and retail sales posted their largest decline in more than a year. Futures pricing before the minutes implied about a 36% chance of a September increase, down from more than 70% at the end of July. The labor market was described in the minutes as stable and balanced, and capital investment and productivity remained strong, so the data do not yet establish contraction. They do explain why the 2-year yield stayed at 4.19% even after the minutes exposed a wider preference for restraint.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's proposal to reduce scheduled policy meetings from eight to six adds a separate uncertainty about reaction speed. The number will not change this year, and fewer meetings could allow more information to accumulate between decisions. It could also make each meeting carry more event risk when energy, tariffs and geopolitical conditions change quickly. The proposal matters less for the August 19 close than the underlying communication problem: investors still have to determine whether Warsh views elevated long yields as useful restraint, a sign of fiscal and credibility risk, or both. Treasury's buyback explicitly sought to lower those yields, creating a policy mix in which the debt manager eases the long end while the central bank keeps a conditional tightening bias.

Market decomposition argues that Wednesday's Treasury action did not loosen the inflation constraint by itself. The 10-year breakeven remained 2.30%, up 4 basis points over 1 week, even as the real yield fell to 2.35%. Brent closed at $91.57, 2.91% higher over 1 week, after the UAE halted trade and financial transactions with Iran following an alleged missile attack; Iran denied responsibility, and flights continued. Saudi Aramco's assurance of full September crude volumes to at least three European refiners supplied a partial physical offset. The mixed WTI and Brent close, together with unchanged breakevens, indicates that energy remained a live tail risk rather than the marginal driver of the Treasury rally.

Housing shows why policymakers cannot treat lower long yields as an abstract market event. The average 30-year mortgage rate remained 6.67%, compared with less than 6% before the Iran conflict, and July pending sales of existing homes matched the second-weakest level in data since 2001. Redfin estimated 51.3% more sellers than buyers, the median existing-home price remained near June's record $434,000, and single-family housing starts were the weakest since 2022. Lower Treasury yields can reduce financing pressure if sustained, but weak transaction volume and residential construction also warn that monetary restraint is already transmitting unevenly. The Fed faces an economy with soft interest-sensitive sectors, strong capital expenditure and unresolved energy inflation, not a single-direction demand signal.

Risk assets made the same distinction. A 0.21% S&P 500 gain and lower VIX show that the buyback did not trigger recession fears. Semiconductor shares fell another 2.12%, extending their 1-week decline to 5.33%, because cheaper government duration does not settle whether AI revenues will justify the associated debt and equity capital. The Dollar Index's fall despite unchanged front-end yields suggests investors attributed the easing to maturity management rather than a cleaner U.S. growth advantage. For the Fed, that weaker currency can itself complicate the inflation path if it persists.

## AI Capital Moves Into New Risk Layers

Alphabet converted a marketed Australian funding plan into a completed A$5.5 billion transaction, providing the clearest current price for a top-quality corporate issuer competing with sovereign duration. Orders exceeded A$18 billion. The company sold A$1 billion of 20-year debt at a 6.98% yield and a spread of 180 basis points over the local benchmark; the largest tranche was a A$1.5 billion floating-rate note, which also attracted the most demand. Compared with the prior day's preliminary guidance, the new information is execution: the debut deal grew above its roughly A$5 billion target, yet the longest tranche still carried Alphabet's highest-ever note yield.

The transaction illustrates both access and transmission. Alphabet has the second-highest S&P rating and one of the strongest corporate balance sheets, so the high absolute yield reflects the global sovereign curve more than an issuer-specific deterioration. At the same time, a highly rated hyperscaler can offer enough incremental yield to redirect core fixed-income demand away from government debt. The company's capital-spending forecast of as much as $205 billion for 2026 and its issuance across U.S. dollars, Swiss francs, sterling, euros, Canadian dollars, yen and now Australian dollars show that the AI funding call is reaching multiple domestic savings pools. Sovereign yields set the base cost; technology supply adds competition above it.

Nebius moved the risk transfer closer to equity. The Amsterdam-based AI cloud company launched $4.5 billion in two convertible series: $2.75 billion due in 2030 with a proposed 0%-0.5% coupon and $1.75 billion due in 2034 with a proposed 4%-4.5% coupon. The offering followed about $4.3 billion of convertible issuance earlier in the year, and the shares fell as much as 9.2% before the U.S. open after rising 197% through Tuesday. Conversion value can lower the cash coupon, but it shifts part of the financing cost into prospective dilution and exposes creditors to the durability of the equity valuation. The deal was still expected to price later Wednesday, so its marketing terms establish funding intent rather than a final clearing level.

Private credit is taking a more structurally subordinated position. Eagle Point Credit Management supplied roughly $1.3 billion of mezzanine debt within a $16 billion financing for Nexus Data Centers' 2,900-acre campus in Hubbard, Texas. Anthropic is the primary tenant, the project includes its own gas-fired power plant, and Google agreed to guarantee the senior debt. Eagle Point's tranche sits below the safest part of the capital structure. The financing began as approximately $150 million of senior secured debt backed by land and expanded repeatedly as the tenant and guarantee package strengthened.

That structure concentrates several dependencies. Construction has to finish, Anthropic has to use the capacity, the dedicated power asset has to operate economically, and Google's guarantee protects the senior layer rather than the mezzanine claim. Developers commonly refinance construction loans after completion, and Nexus may seek high-yield bonds later in the year to refinance the $15 billion bank-led portion. The project can therefore migrate from private construction risk into public credit after physical completion, leaving ultimate loss allocation dependent on guarantee scope, collateral value and refinancing conditions.

The aggregate calendar remains large enough to compete with sovereign supply even after Wednesday's rally. U.S. investment-grade issuance reached $152 billion for August, a third consecutive monthly record, while European borrowers placed at least EUR38.5 billion this week, the busiest post-summer restart on record. European investment-grade spreads were 77 basis points at Tuesday's close, tighter than at the end of June, and strong fund inflows allowed Finland, Sika, Mizuho and others to issue despite the government-bond selloff. The market has not shut. Investors are demanding appropriate concessions and increasingly choosing whether to take duration, corporate credit, project execution, conversion or subordination risk.

Broad returns on August 19 rewarded the duration component. A U.S. 20-plus-year AAA-A corporate bond index gained 1.61%, the comparable BBB index rose 1.51%, and a developed-market 10-plus-year investment-grade dollar index advanced 1.35%. Those moves were smaller than the 1.69% gain in the long Treasury index and do not establish spread tightening. They show that Treasury's intervention lifted long corporate bonds through the benchmark channel while leaving issuer and structure selection unresolved.

The proposed $1.15 billion Digital Drive bond adds a future test at the weaker end of the tenant spectrum. The Virginia data center is leased to speculative-grade CoreWeave, and comparable CoreWeave-linked project debt has required materially higher yields than financings backed by blue-chip hyperscalers; Galaxy Digital paid 10% on a $3.5 billion deal in July. The September sale remains prospective, but it frames the next question for AI credit: whether benchmark relief can lower project coupons when tenant credit, concentration and construction risk remain unchanged.

## Policy Divergence and Creditor Control

Indonesia delivered a realized policy result rather than the expected hold described before the meeting. Acting Governor Destry Damayanti kept the BI-Rate at 5.75% for a second month after 100 basis points of increases this year. She reaffirmed currency stability as the priority, expanded a hedging incentive program effective in the second week of September, and said the central bank would continue onshore and offshore intervention while using macroprudential tools to support lending. The rupiah ended 0.1% stronger and the 10-year government yield fell 5 basis points to 7.11%, its lowest in almost two months.

The decision represents continuity with a change in instruments. Bank Indonesia wants to attract foreign currency without raising yields on SRBI securities, whose 12-month average yield fell 22 basis points on August 14 as outstanding issuance was reduced. Credit growth reached 13.58% in July, the fastest since at least the pandemic, giving the bank reason to avoid draining more domestic liquidity. The approach lowers the immediate probability of another policy increase while keeping rupiah defense explicit. It also leaves a clear vulnerability: renewed dollar strength or higher U.S. yields could force the new leadership to choose between cheaper domestic liquidity and currency credibility.

South Africa received a cleaner disinflation surprise. July headline inflation slowed to 4.3% from 5.0%, below the 4.5% consensus, and monthly inflation eased to 0.2% from 0.7%. Goods inflation fell to 3.4% from 4.8%, services eased to 5.0% from 5.2%, and food inflation dropped to 0.6%, its lowest since 2010. Core inflation moved the other way, edging to 4.2% from 4.1% year on year, so the result supports patience rather than an unconditional easing turn. The 10-year government yield fell 2 basis points to 8.68%; forward-rate agreements still assigned a 70% probability to a 25-basis-point increase at the September 23 meeting.

India's August 3-5 minutes also favored waiting, though from a more explicitly hawkish starting point. The six-member committee unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25% and retained a neutral stance for a fourth meeting. Governor Sanjay Malhotra emphasized the risk that food, fuel and other input costs could broaden, and Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta said a hike could become necessary later in the year as inflation is projected to reach 5.9% in the October-December quarter. The RBI raised its fiscal-year growth forecast to 6.7% and lowered its inflation forecast to 5%, preserving room to observe the energy shock rather than react immediately.

Korea's curve shows the market consequence when long-end inflation concern outruns expected central-bank action. The 3s10s spread reached almost 54 basis points, its widest since October 2021, after the 10-year yield rose about 90 basis points from the end of February. The 3-year yield had already fallen 13 basis points from its late-July peak as investors questioned whether the Bank of Korea would follow July's 25-basis-point increase with aggressive tightening. Oil dependence and the global sovereign selloff keep term compensation high even as LS Securities expects only one more increase this year and a 3.25% terminal rate in the first half of 2027.

Emerging-market credit supplied two different examples of idiosyncratic resilience. Egypt's sovereign dollar spread reached 322 basis points at the end of the prior week, its lowest since 2014 and roughly 150 basis points tighter since March. Record reserves of $56.3 billion, a more flexible pound, remittances, tourism, Suez Canal receipts and $1.8 billion released after an IMF review have reduced acute external-funding risk. High gross financing needs and slow privatization remain constraints, and the rally leaves less valuation cushion. Ukraine's 2029 notes, by contrast, yielded 13% and traded near 85 cents after rising from 58 cents in June 2025. European approval of a EUR90 billion loan, military adaptation and creditor restructurings have improved the perceived funding runway, but debt is projected to reach 110% of GDP by 2027 and attacks threaten to halve grain exports. Its 12% sovereign return this year is compensation for war and restructuring outcomes, not a lower-risk version of the Egypt trade.

Private-credit losses made creditor control tangible away from AI. HPS, now owned by BlackRock, and Oaktree took control of MBS Group by converting as much as $900 million of debt into approximately $100 million of equity and committing another $40 million. HPS held a $600 million first lien and Oaktree a $300 million junior lien. The restructuring displaced Hackman Capital Partners and Affinius Capital after higher borrowing costs, weaker film production and the 2023 labor strikes impaired studio economics. Debt reduction restores operating capacity, but the conversion also reveals the severity of enterprise-value loss and shifts recovery from contractual claims to ownership of a cyclical production-services business.

These sovereign and corporate cases resist a single global-duration conclusion. Indonesia is defending a currency with incentives and targeted instruments; South Africa received headline disinflation with sticky core prices; India is waiting through an energy shock; Korea is pricing oil and term premium beyond the likely policy path; Egypt has rebuilt external buffers; Ukraine is trading on aid and war outcomes; MBS creditors have taken the company. Lower U.S. long yields improve the common discount-rate backdrop, but local policy credibility, cash-flow control, collateral and refinancing structure still determine who benefits.

## Forward Market Significance

The durability of Treasury's intervention now depends on whether the announced purchases change clearing prices after the initial short covering. The September 9 start, the eventual size of each 10- to 30-year operation, bill issuance used to finance it and any revision to long-coupon auction guidance will reveal whether the program remains a bounded liquidity measure or becomes active maturity management. A sustained long-end rally with stable bill funding and heavy two-way cash turnover would show that modest duration removal can attract private buyers back. A return of the 30-year yield toward its pre-announcement high despite larger operations would shift attention back to the $40.05 trillion debt stock, the $1.17 trillion interest bill and the credibility cost of repeated surprise intervention.

The next inflation and policy sequence has to reconcile the July Fed minutes with weaker subsequent activity. Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks and the next labor, retail and inflation releases need to show whether the three voting dissents and two hawkish nonvoters represent a durable tightening coalition or a position overtaken by softer data. Continued weakness in hiring and consumption with stable core prices would validate the unchanged 2-year yield and allow the real-yield rally to broaden. Persistent services inflation, a weaker dollar or Brent moving decisively above the current $91.57 close would reconnect the front end with the long end and expose the tension between Treasury easing financial conditions and the Fed's inflation mandate.

Japan's August 20 20-year auction is the nearest external test of whether U.S. relief can travel across sovereign curves. The yield entered the sale near 3.775%, still close to July's 3.89% peak, with a September BOJ increase carrying roughly a three-quarters market probability and domestic institutions cautious about superlong duration. Bid-to-cover, tail and secondary performance will distinguish demand drawn by absolute yield from temporary relief imported from Treasuries. Strong absorption would show that official U.S. support can reopen global duration at sufficiently high yields; weak demand would confirm that Japan's monetary normalization, fiscal stance and buyer retrenchment remain independent pressures even after the U.S. curve flattens.
